title: ～ていただけませんか — “could you please ～?” (very polite)
summary: A far more polite way to ask than ～てください. Add いただけませんか to the te-form. Used with superiors and customers.

patterns.form: 動詞て形＋いただけませんか
patterns.gloss: Verb te-form + いただけませんか

body.p: It uses the negative potential いただけない of the humble いただく (to receive), meaning “could I not receive the favor of ～?” The negative leaves the listener room to refuse, which makes it polite.
For asking someone to take a photo or open a window, and similar favors. A slightly less formal version is ～てもらえませんか.

examples.ja: ここで写真（しゃしん）を撮（と）っていただけませんか。
examples.romaji: Koko de shashin o totte itadakemasen ka.
examples.tr: Could you please take a photo here?

examples.ja: 少（すこ）し窓（まど）を開（あ）けていただけませんか。
examples.romaji: Sukoshi mado o akete itadakemasen ka.
examples.tr: Could you please open the window a little?

examples.ja: もう一度（いちど）ゆっくり説明（せつめい）していただけませんか。
examples.romaji: Mō ichido yukkuri setsumei shite itadakemasen ka.
examples.tr: Could you please explain it slowly one more time?

pitfalls: The speaker is asking; attach it to the action you want from the other person.
Ending with ～ていただきます makes it a statement, not a request.
